Andrzejewo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Andrzejewo-Kolonie, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Andrzejewo began in the 19th century; population reached 48% (580) by 1880, declining to 28% (277) by 1921, mostly murdered by Nazis in 1941 at Mianówek and Szumowo. This cemetery, likely established mid-19th century alongside broader religious-facility regulation, was formally closed on October 9, 1964, with documentation noting it had been 'defunct since 1939, fallen into disrepair and not maintained.' A 1988 cemetery survey found the layout entirely unclear and everything 'deeply degraded,' with the grounds also used for cattle and horse grazing.
